changed_in.5.2: Two environment variable names are consulted at start-up where there was one. Lua reads `LUA_CPATH_5_2` first, falls back to `LUA_CPATH`, and settles for the default compiled into the interpreter only if neither is set; earlier versions read `LUA_CPATH` and nothing else. The same version added a way to refuse the environment outright — the stand-alone interpreter's `-E` option builds this string from the compiled-in default and reads neither name — and it does that through a field in the registry, so a program embedding Lua can ask for the same thing.
changed_in.5.4: Where the value came from an environment variable, only the first `;;` in it is replaced by the compiled-in default. Earlier versions replace every `;;`, so a setting carrying two of them ends up holding the whole default path twice.
